questions.text: Why can a lower-priced cryptocurrency still have a larger market size than a higher-priced one?
options: Because market cap is price multiplied by circulating supply, so a lower price can still yield a larger market cap if the supply is sufficiently high.
Because price alone determines market capitalization.
Because higher-priced coins always have larger market caps.
Because trading volume overrides market cap considerations.
questions.explanation: Market cap equals price multiplied by circulating supply, so total market size depends on both price and supply: a lower price can still mean a larger market if the circulating supply is high enough.

questions.text: Which pattern indicates an uptrend in price?
options: Sideways movement with equal highs and lows
Sharp spikes followed by immediate declines
questions.explanation: An uptrend is a series of higher highs and higher lows, like climbing a staircase.

questions.text: True or false: You should build a personal watchlist of three to five reputable assets and follow them for weeks instead of chasing every trend.
questions.explanation: True. Pick three to five reputable assets, watch how they move over several weeks, and stop chasing every passing trend.

questions.text: If you answer 'no' to any question in your pre‑trade checklist (understand the asset, use money you can afford to leave untouched, check it fits your plan), what should you do?
options: Increase your position size to compensate for uncertainty.
Ignore the checklist and rely on market sentiment.
Pause and step back from placing the order.
questions.explanation: If you answer no to any checklist question, you pause and step back instead of placing the order.
